gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.hint: person needed (-ist for fields of study)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ist forms the person who studies a subject: biology becomes biologist.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: The audience found the lecture extremely ___ (BORE).
gaps.explanation: The lecture causes boredom, so it is boring; the audience would be bored.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: She apologized for the ___ caused by the delay (CONVENIENT).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — the delay was a bad thing
gaps.explanation: A delay causes inconvenience (negative prefix in- + noun); the sentence needs the noun, not the adjectives.
